newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property stocks fall on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property stocks fall on rumours.

text.p: Singapore property counters fell in late trading on Friday on rumours that new rules will be announced on public housing, stockbroking analysts and dealers said.
The rumours triggered selling in property stocks including City Developments, down 40 cents to S$12.80, DBS Land down 15 cents to S$5.10 and and Wing Tai Holdings down 20 cents to S$4.20.
The selling pulled the SES property index down 2.61 percent or 18.78 points to 699.76.
The rumours said the government Housing Development Board (HDB) would announce the sweeping changes to the public housing market.
A HDB spokeswoman told Reuters that Minister for National Development Lim Hng Kiang would hold a news conference at 11 a.m. (0300 GMT) on Saturday.
She said the conference would be open only to local media and refused to say what it would address.
Analysts said some of the changes could include higher interest rates for buyers who want to upgrade to a bigger public housing unit.
The other rumour was that HDB owners would have to stay longer in their public housing units before they being allowed to sell them.
A property analyst said the changes would have an adverse impact on the prices of private housing as the two markets are linked.
